links.comparator_used: label-only prompt without a required verbatim supporting quote
links.outcome: coverage and conditional macro-F1 for trial eligibility-scope classification
links.effect: Coverage fell: GPT-5.2 86.2% to 84.3%, Gemini 98.3% to 92.8%, Claude 96.0% to 94.5%. Conditional macro-F1 changed by model: slight gains for GPT-5.2 and Gemini, a decrease for Claude. Labels were stable across repetitions (Fleiss' kappa 0.829 to 0.969).
links.tradeoff: More abstentions and, for Gemini, more invalid outputs. Quotes introduce new failure modes: only 48.0% to 78.8% of evidence-bearing predictions were judged semantically supported.
links.quote: Evidence requirements modestly reduced coverage (GPT-5.2 86.2% to 84.3%, Gemini 98.3% to 92.8%, Claude 96.0% to 94.5%) by increasing abstentions and, for Gemini, invalid outputs.

links.comparator_used: all predictions released without checking the quote against the source (unrestricted predictions)
links.outcome: macro-F1 versus coverage when restricting to predictions with supported quotes
links.effect: Mechanically valid quotes occurred in 83.3% to 91.2% of runs, but only 48.0% to 78.8% of evidence-bearing predictions were judged semantically supported. Restricting to supported predictions raised macro-F1.
links.tradeoff: Lower coverage. Valid substring quotes were often not semantically supportive of the label.
links.quote: Restricting to supported predictions increased macro-F1 at the cost of lower coverage.

design_hint: verbatim evidence quotation and automated verification guardrail
